analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report, November 20, 2026 (Friday 11/13 – Thursday 11/19)
key_insights: The GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell -1.59% from 11/13 to 11/19 versus MSCI World TR -5.24%. Beta contributed -2.43%, partly offset by alpha of +0.84% from gains on both the short and long sides.
The GS Equity Systematic L/S Performance Estimate was roughly flat (-0.01%) over the same week. Negative alpha from long side losses was offset by a roughly equal positive beta contribution.

Overall book gross leverage rose 3.8 pts to 315.9% (89th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 1.3 pts to 70.1% (2nd percentile 1-year). The overall L/S ratio fell 1.5% to 1.570 (2nd percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 3.6 pts to 204.8% (13th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 3.1 pts to 42.3% (1st percentile 1-year).
Beta-adjusted fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 8.3 pts to 214.2%, a 1-year low. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell 8.8 pts to 48.2%, a 5-year low.

Global equities were net sold for a 3rd straight week (-1.0 SDs 1-year). Gross trading activity rose for the first time in 6 weeks and at the fastest pace in 2.5 months, with short sales outpacing long buys 1.5 to 1.
This week's shorting activity was the largest since April 2025.
All major regions were net sold, led in dollar terms by EM Asia and Europe. By standardized flow, North America long buys were +3.17 SDs and EM short sales were -3.04 SDs.
Single stocks were net sold for a 10th straight week, driven by short sales. Macro products were net bought for a 5th straight week, driven by long buys.
10 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by Financials, Info Tech and Consumer Discretionary. Energy was the only net bought sector, with long buys of +1.96 SDs.

Financials was the most net sold global sector. It was net sold for a 7th straight week and at the fastest pace in 8 months, with short sales outpacing long buys 4.5 to 1. Short sales in Financials were -3.31 SDs.

Financials selling was concentrated in North America (short sales) and Europe (short and long sales). Within the sector, selling in Banks, Insurance and Financial Services outpaced modest buying in Consumer Finance. DM Asia was the exception to the regional selling.

The Prime book is underweight Financials versus MSCI World by -4.3% (66th percentile 1-year, 24th percentile 5-year). Gross/Net allocations to Financials are 13.0%/13.0% of the global Prime book (92nd/72nd percentiles 1-year, 51st/48th percentiles 5-year).
risk_factors: Net selling for a 3rd straight week and a 10th straight week in single stocks, led by short sales, shows hedge funds are adding downside exposure.
Net leverage near 1-year and multi-year lows alongside gross leverage in the 89th percentile indicates books are more heavily hedged but still carry large gross exposure.
